findings.problem: The file proves the same five-lemma chain twice. The inner-product version `HasSecondOrderExpansionAt u x p B` is at lines 26–106, and the continuous-linear-functional version `HasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM u x ℓ B` is at lines 108–189. The two chains differ only in the first-order coefficient, `inner ℝ p v` versus `ℓ v`. The proof bodies are otherwise identical. Both build `htend : Tendsto (fun t => t • v) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 0)` and compose with `comp_tendsto`. Both apply the same `simp [lineRestriction, real_inner_smul_right, ...]` `congr_left` step. Both rescale `‖t • v‖ ^ 2` to `‖t‖ ^ 2` via `norm_smul` and `of_const_mul_right`. Both prove the shifted version with the same `hpoint : x + (t + z) • v = x + t • v + z • v` argument. The two definitions in Foundation/SecondOrder.lean differ only in whether the linear term is `inner ℝ p z` or `ℓ z`, but no bridge from the inner-product form to the CLM form is used here. The existing `hasSecondOrderExpansionAt_of_clm_eq_inner` goes only from the CLM form to the inner-product form. As a result, any fix to the little-o rescaling or the shift argument has to be made in two places.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep the CLM chain as the only full proof. Add a bridge lemma in Foundation/SecondOrder.lean or at the top of this file:

```lean
theorem hasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM_innerSL {u : E → ℝ} {x p : E} {B : E →L[ℝ] E}
    (h : HasSecondOrderExpansionAt u x p B) :
    HasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM u x (innerSL ℝ p) B := by
  refine h.congr_left ?_
  intro z
  simp [innerSL_apply_apply]
```

The proof sketch is that the two expansions differ only by the pointwise identity `innerSL ℝ p z = inner ℝ p z`, which is `innerSL_apply_apply`.

Then rewrite the five inner-product lemmas as corollaries, with the same hypotheses and statements as now. For example:

```lean
theorem HasSecondOrderExpansionAt.lineRestriction_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt
    {u : E → ℝ} {x p : E} {B : E →L[ℝ] E}
    (h : HasSecondOrderExpansionAt u x p B) (v : E) :
    HasSecondOrderExpansionAt (lineRestriction u x v) 0 (inner ℝ p v)
      ((inner ℝ v (B v)) • (1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ)) := by
  simpa [innerSL_apply_apply] using
    (hasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM_innerSL h).lineRestriction_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt v

theorem HasSecondOrderExpansionAt.lineRestriction_at_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt
    {u : E → ℝ} {x p v : E} {B : E →L[ℝ] E} {t : ℝ}
    (h : HasSecondOrderExpansionAt u (x + t • v) p B) :
    HasSecondOrderExpansionAt (lineRestriction u x v) t (inner ℝ p v)
      ((inner ℝ v (B v)) • (1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ)) := by
  simpa [innerSL_apply_apply] using
    (hasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM_innerSL h).lineRestriction_at_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt
```

The `_isLittleO`, `_of_norm_eq_one` and `_standard` variants follow the same pattern, each one line plus `simpa [innerSL_apply_apply]`. Alternatively, restate the three auxiliary little-o lemmas once for the CLM form and delete the inner-product copies, since only `lineRestriction_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt` is used downstream (Reconstruction.lean, e.g. line 306). The names used elsewhere are unchanged.
findings.benefit: About 80 lines of duplicated asymptotic reasoning shrink to one copy plus short corollaries. A future change to the rescaling or shifting argument is made once. A reader can see that the inner-product and CLM versions are the same statement, instead of comparing two near-identical proofs line by line. The new bridge lemma also complements the existing `hasSecondOrderExpansionAt_of_clm_eq_inner`, which currently covers only one direction.
